results.correct_value: No glacier travel, but a crevasse-like moat between snow and rock at the North Col must be crossed and widens as summer goes on
results.evidence: An accident report describes a climber falling into a ~20-ft-deep moat between the snow slope and rock at ~6,680 ft on the North Col descent in August. A July 2025 trip report found a seven-foot-deep gap with water running in it at the col, and the Mazamas route text warns the step across the moat can be intimidating or impossible.

patches.expect: N/A - no glacier travel on this route
patches.value: No glacier travel, but the moat between the snow and the rock at the North Col is a crevasse-like gap that must be crossed both ways; it widens as the season goes on and can be many feet deep by late summer.

results.correct_value: Jun-Sep, best in June to early July before the moat opens
results.evidence: The peak description gives the season as roughly May to the first autumn snow and says crossing the moat can be challenging from early July on, with the col gully becoming a talus slog once the snow is gone. The Mazamas route text notes the later in the season, the lower the snow and the worse the moat step; a late-July 2026 trip report found hard, thin snow over an open moat where thick early-season snow had made it straightforward, and a 1979 accident was a fall into the moat in late August. So the row's best_season, pro_tips, approach_variants, itinerary.cal and climate are right and season/seasonal_guidance were the outliers.

July.reason: Route becomes viable as snow starts clearing, but lingering snowfields on approach/upper slopes and afternoon thunderstorms are common early in the month

August.reason: Most consistent snow-free conditions and the most stable weather window for the summit scramble

September.reason: Cooler, generally stable, but shorter days and possible early-season snow late in the month

June.reason: Snow still covers the North Col talus and usually bridges the moat at the chimney's base; steep snow to the col needs an axe and crampons, and Barlow Pass can still hold snow early in the month

July.reason: Snow thins on the approach and the moat begins to open, more so late in the month; afternoon thunderstorms are common

August.reason: The steadiest weather, but the moat at the chimney is often open and awkward or impassable, and the talus below the col is loose once melted out

September.reason: Cooler and generally stable, but shorter days, an open moat and possible early-season snow late in the month
